current_answer: A new working-paper abstract reports 20% more startup formation in industries with higher generative-AI task exposure than in less-exposed industries after the technology spread. It also reports industry-level employment and wage growth from new entrants, despite smaller individual startups. This is a possible job-creation channel, not proof that AI caused the growth or that existing workers gained. Separately, U.S. junior software ads weakened relative to senior ads, but they did not count hires or isolate AI. The evidence still does not support one universal verdict on jobs.

catalogue_card.question: Could AI create firms even while entry jobs shrink?
catalogue_card.text: A CEPR abstract reports 20% more startup formation in more GenAI-exposed industries. It also reports entry-linked job growth, but does not prove AI caused a net gain for workers.

summary: A new CEPR abstract reports 20% more startup formation in industries with higher generative-AI task exposure after diffusion.
It reports industry-level employment and wage growth from new entry despite smaller individual startups.
The accessible abstract does not establish AI causation or show what happened to incumbents and displaced workers.
A separate U.S. junior-software vacancy warning remains; startup entry and job ads are different outcomes.
uncertainty: Only the CEPR abstract and author summary were inspected; full methods and precise labor estimates were not available.
The abstract does not specify geography or enough detail to rule out concurrent industry trends.
Industry exposure is not observed AI adoption by each startup; new-firm gains are not a personal job forecast.
freshness_note: Checked 3 October 2026. Added a startup-entry counter-signal from a September working-paper abstract; it is not a verified net jobs estimate.
